news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed Memora, a harmonic memory representation that balances abstraction and specificity. This technology aims to improve AI agents' ability to remember past conversations and tasks, increasing efficiency as tasks become longer and more complex.
news.enterprise_use: Check your Microsoft 365 or Azure integration to see if Memora-based memory solutions can enhance AI-powered chatbots, virtual assistants, or other conversational interfaces. Missing this means relying on inefficient context retrieval methods, negatively impacting user experience and potentially increasing support requests. Memora can be directly integrated with your existing SSO providers, endpoint security tools, and AI platforms.

news.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research introduced SkillOpt: an AI system that turns agent skill editing into a trainable process, improving agent behavior reliability without modifying model weights. This AI development enhances the reliability of AI agent behavior and potentially reduces the need for manual tuning.
